item.title: Council tees up expansion to rent protection program
item.dc:creator: Ben Miller
item.description:
A broadly popular program that freezes rents for senior and disabled tenants by providing property tax credits to landlords is likely to cover more applicants, after the City Council voiced broad support for bills that would raise renters’ income limits to $75,000. At a Friday hearing lawmakers discussed proposed changes to Senior Citizen and Disability Rent Increase Exemptions, two programs they framed as a mutual benefit that more tenants and owners should be utilizing. The expansion of the program, part of a larger package of housing bills, is likely to pass at an upcoming stated meeting of City Council, though […]

item.title: Former Hudson Yards hotel sold in foreclosure auction
item.dc:creator: TRD Staff
item.description:
A 12-story property in Hudson Yards previously owned by Solly Assa changed hands at a foreclosure auction, inviting speculation over the next iteration of the building. Investment banker Capital Insight acquired 511 Ninth Avenue through a foreclosure auction through a credit bid at a price between $68 million and $71.3 million, the Commercial Observer reported. Capital Insight was the lender and debt holder on the property, which has a troubled history. item.title: Borough Developers buys site for trio of 99-unit DoBro buildings
item.dc:creator: TRD Staff
item.description:
Borough Developers is ready to bring the next set of 99-unit buildings to New York City after buying a Downtown Brooklyn site. Shimon Kleinman’s firm purchased the Bridge & Fulton Development Site from ICER Real Estate for $83.5 million, the Commercial Observer reported. The site consists of 485 Fulton Street, plus 147 Lawrence Street. JLL’s Ethan Stanton, Michael Mazzara and Brendan Maddigan represented both sides of the transaction. Borough Developers also landed an $85 million acquisition and pre-development loan from BridgeCity Capital. “The combination of scale, location and development flexibility made 485 Fulton particularly compelling,” Mazzara said in a statement […]

item.title: More details emerge for Jacob Schwimmer’s LIC development
item.dc:creator: TRD Staff
item.description:
Developer Jacob Schwimmer and JCS Realty Group filed plans for a 495-unit residential project in Long Island City, Queens this month, but didn’t appear to own the necessary site. They still don’t, but they have a deal with a buyer who does. Texas-based Montgomery Street Partners acquired the site at 10-01 45th Road from the heirs of Dieter Holterbosch for $95 million, Crain’s reported. The deal for the 80,000-square-foot site breaks down to $1,188 per square foot. In addition to acquiring the site, Montgomery Street entered into a lease agreement with JCS, which will develop the site that once housed […]

item.title: NY Dirt: How New York steered 4 buildings to a nonprofit over other buyers
item.dc:creator: Lilah Burke
item.description:
Four troubled Brooklyn buildings have a new landlord.  After intervention from the city and the state Office of the Attorney General, that landlord is the nonprofit organization IMPACCT Brooklyn.  The city and state AG helped steer a bankruptcy process toward IMPACCT and away from two other bidders, both for-profit entities offering double the cash.  Mayor Zohran Mamdani has made transfers to “high-road landlords,” including nonprofit corporations, a key part of his housing plan. But the story at the four properties demonstrates how the city and state have worked to steer sales even before his tenure.  The recent history with the […]

item.title: Acore takes control of Beacon Capital’s Hell’s Kitchen life science development
item.dc:creator: Keith Larsen
item.description:
Acore Capital has put an end to Beacon Capital Partners’ plans to build a life science development in Hell’s Kitchen. The lender took control of two office buildings at 707 11th Avenue and 615 West 50th Street that were once used as Kenneth Cole’s headquarters and more recently pegged for a 185,000-square-foot life science development. The sale was a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure, according to property records. The transfer value of the sale was $60 million, per records. PincusCo first reported the news. Beacon Capital Partners and CalSTRS partnered with Georgetown to buy the properties from SL Green for $95 million […]

item.title: Former Disney CEO buys Sherry-Netherland co-op for $10M
item.dc:creator: Sheridan Wall, Mary Diduch
item.description:
Former Disney CEO Michael Eisner and his wife, Jane, dropped $10 million on a co-op at the Sherry-Netherland.  The couple purchased an apartment at 781 Fifth Avenue in an off-market deal from a trust tied to Edythe Broad, an art collector, philanthropist and widow of developer Eli Broad, according to public records.  The trade was in line with other deals for full-floor apartments in the building’s tower, including Unit 27T, which sold for $9.4 million in 2023, and Unit 35T, which sold for $9.5 million that same year, according to Streeteasy.  Eli Broad’s ties to the Upper East Side hotel […]

item.title: Comptroller follows through with $300M affordable housing investment
item.dc:creator: TRD Staff
item.description:
Last spring, New York City Comptroller Mark Levine’s unveiled plans to use the city’s public pension funds to invest $4 billion over the next four years in affordable housing development. Levine is making the first allocation in that plan. The municipal pension funds are investing $300 million into the AFL-CIO Housing Investment Trust, Gothamist reported. The trust has helped to build more than 44,000 units in the city in the last four decades and has another 10,000 units in the financing pipeline, including an unnamed Brooklyn co-op development. “This is a dramatic increase in the pace of investment because the […]

item.title: ZD Jasper makes biggest condo bet yet in LIC
item.dc:creator: Jake Indursky
item.description:
ZD Jasper is making its biggest bet yet on the Long Island City condo market.  The Great Neck-based developer launched sales Wednesday at the Paragon, a 182-unit building at 45-40 Vernon Boulevard, making it one of the first condo projects on the LIC waterfront in over a decade.  A Serhant New Development team led by Kayla Lee is leading sales at the building. Lee said that 30 percent of the units were already in contract before sales launched this week.  ZD Jasper bought the site in 2024 for $47 million from Quadrum Global, Baron Property Group and Simon Development. item.title: Meet the Stellbergers, the mysterious brothers hipsterizing rundown real estate
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Cryan, Matthew Elo
item.description:
Two former soccer-star brothers from Colorado have built a niche buying run-down properties and giving them a hipster makeover. Now, they may be bringing their formula to Carroll Gardens. Dawson and Wells Stellberger are the names behind Happier Grocery, the buzzy Soho market that has grown into a community and event space with a distinctly downtown vibe.
